requirements.statement: The platform will allow XATA employees to create, manage, prioritize, track and complete personal and team TODO items.
Provide a single centralized web application for managing TODO items.
XATA wants the first release to be intentionally small and easy to use.
Allow users to quickly create and update TODOs.
Provide visibility of open, completed and overdue work.
Allow team members to assign TODOs to one another.
Provide basic priority and due-date management.
Provide a simple dashboard for work tracking.
System shall allow an authenticated user to create a TODO. (Priority: Must)
A TODO shall contain title, description, status, priority and due date. (Priority: Must)
Users shall be able to edit TODOs they own or are authorized to manage. (Priority: Must)
Users shall be able to assign a TODO to another authorized user. (Priority: Must)
System shall support Open, In Progress and Completed statuses. (Priority: Must)
System shall support Low, Medium, High and Critical priorities. (Priority: Must)
Users shall filter TODOs by status, priority, assignee and due date. (Priority: Must)
Users shall search TODOs by title or description. (Priority: Should)
System shall provide user login and a basic user profile.
Users shall be able to view and delete TODOs.
Users shall be able to add an optional notes field to a TODO.
System shall provide a dashboard showing TODO status.
System shall provide a basic team view of assigned TODOs.
System shall maintain audit information for TODOs, including created date and updated date.
Employee role shall be able to create and manage own TODOs.
Employee role shall be able to view assigned TODOs.
Employee role shall be able to update the status of TODOs.
Team Lead role shall be able to create and assign TODOs.
Team Lead role shall be able to view team TODOs.
Team Lead role shall be able to monitor overdue work.
Administrator role shall be able to manage users and basic platform configuration.
Dashboard shall show Open, In Progress, Completed and Overdue counts. (priority: Must; section 7.3 also lists total open, in-progress, completed, and overdue TODOs)
Team Leads shall view TODOs assigned to their team members. (priority: Must)
System shall maintain created-by, created-date, updated-by and updated-date for each TODO. (priority: Must)
Users shall be able to delete TODOs where permitted (BR-013 wording) or authorized (section 7.2 wording). (priority: Should)
System shall prevent unauthorized modification of another user's TODO. (priority: Must)
System shall provide a web interface through supported browsers. (priority: Must)
Dashboard shall show High/Critical priority TODOs.
Users shall be able to create a TODO by entering a title, entering a description, selecting a priority, selecting a due date, and saving the TODO.
When creating a TODO, users may optionally assign it to a user.
Users shall be able to view TODO details.
Users shall be able to edit TODO information.
Users shall be able to change TODO status.
Users shall be able to change TODO priority or due date.
Users shall be able to reassign TODOs where authorized.
A TODO must have a title.
A due date cannot be earlier than the creation date unless explicitly permitted.
Completed TODOs must have Completed status.
Only authorized users can assign or modify TODOs.
A TODO is overdue when its due date has passed and its status is not Completed.
Deleting a TODO must not delete the user account or other TODOs.
Users can log in and create a TODO.
A TODO can be assigned, updated and completed.
Dashboard counts correctly reflect TODO state.
Users cannot modify TODOs outside their authorization.
Filtering and search return correct results.
The application meets agreed NFRs.
XATA can complete the core TODO lifecycle without administrator assistance.
Normal page/API response time must be ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests under normal load.
TODO create/update operations must complete in ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests.
Dashboard loading must complete in ≤ 3 seconds for 95% of requests.
Search/filter response must be ≤ 2 seconds for 95% of requests.
The platform must support at least 500 concurrent active users.
Monthly availability shall be ≥ 99.5%, excluding agreed maintenance windows.
Planned maintenance shall be communicated at least 24 hours in advance.
Service shall be restored within 30 minutes after application failure.
The solution shall support growth in users and TODO volume without major redesign.
The solution shall support at least 100,000 TODO records initially.
Application services should be horizontally scalable where practical.
Database design shall support future growth beyond initial capacity.
All users shall be authenticated before protected functionality.
Authorization shall be role-based.
Users shall only access TODO data permitted by their role.
Data shall be encrypted in transit using HTTPS/TLS.
Sensitive credentials shall not be hard-coded.
If passwords are locally managed, they shall use secure industry-standard hashing.
The application shall protect against common web vulnerabilities including injection, broken access control and XSS.
Administrative actions should be auditable.
TODO records shall have unique identifiers.
Required fields shall be validated server-side.
Updates shall not silently overwrite conflicting data.
Created and updated timestamps shall be stored consistently.
Referential integrity shall be maintained between TODOs and users.
Deleted data handling shall follow XATA's retention policy.
Core create/update/complete flow should require minimal steps.
UI shall be responsive for standard desktop and tablet screens.
Validation errors shall be understandable.
Status, priority and overdue items shall be visually distinguishable.
Common actions shall be discoverable without technical knowledge.
Target WCAG 2.1 AA principles where practical.
Keyboard navigation should support core workflows.
Form controls should have meaningful labels.
Text should have sufficient contrast and readable sizing.
Solution shall use modular, maintainable code.
Business logic shall be separated from presentation and persistence.
APIs and major components shall be documented.
Automated unit tests shall cover critical business logic.
Configuration shall be externalized from source code.
Logging shall support troubleshooting without exposing sensitive information.
Application errors shall be logged with sufficient troubleshooting context.
Health checks shall be available.
Key metrics should include request failures and response latency.
Logs should include correlation/request identifiers where appropriate.
Operational alerts should be configurable for service failures.
Production data shall be backed up according to an agreed schedule.
Backups shall be protected from unauthorized access.
Solution shall support restoration after major failure.
Target RPO is 15 minutes, unless XATA agrees otherwise.
Target RTO is 30 minutes.
Support current versions of major enterprise browsers such as Chrome and Edge.
Avoid browser-specific functionality unless approved.
APIs should use documented, versionable interfaces.
Collect only data required for TODO management.
Access to personal/team information shall follow XATA authorization rules.
Sensitive information shall not be written to application logs.
Data retention and deletion shall follow XATA policy.
Critical application/database components shall have documented recovery procedures.
Recovery procedures shall be tested periodically.
XBS shall document dependencies required to restore the service.
XBS shall demonstrate compliance with agreed NFRs through appropriate testing, evidence, configuration review and operational validation before production acceptance.
The Security NFR category has a priority of Must.
The Performance NFR category has a priority of Must.
The Availability NFR category has a priority of Must.
The Data Integrity NFR category has a priority of Must.
The Backup & Recovery NFR category has a priority of Must.
The Usability NFR category has a priority of Must.
The Maintainability NFR category has a priority of Must.
The Accessibility NFR category has a priority of Should.
The Advanced observability NFR category has a priority of Should.
Users shall be able to mark TODOs as completed.

open_questions.question: The evidence contains business objectives and background statements but no formal requirements section, requirement IDs, or non-functional requirement evidence. Should the objective statements be treated as binding requirements, and are any NFRs (performance, security, availability, accessibility, etc.) defined elsewhere?
The objective 'Reduce dependency on spreadsheets, email and chat for TODO tracking' is an outcome rather than a testable system behaviour. Is it a requirement, and if so, how is it measured?
'Quickly' (create and update TODOs) has no defined threshold or unit of time. What response or completion time is expected?
'Overdue' work is referenced but not defined. What rule determines an item is overdue (for example, due date passed and not completed, and in which time zone)?
The scope of 'team' and the rules for assigning TODOs (for example, who may assign, whether assignment is restricted to a team, and whether assignees must accept) are not defined.
'Basic' priority and due-date management and a 'simple' dashboard are not specified. What priority levels, due-date behaviours, and dashboard content are required for the first release?

The intended users and access model are not defined beyond 'XATA employees' (for example, whether personal TODOs are private and whether team visibility is shared across the organisation). Who can view, edit, or complete items owned by others?
What defines an 'authorized' user or 'authorized to manage' a TODO, and which roles or permissions govern edit and assignment rights (BR-003, BR-005)?
Is an optional notes field required in addition to the description, since BR-002 lists the TODO fields without notes but scope section 4.1 includes optional notes?
What is the definition of 'overdue' for the Team Lead's monitoring responsibility, and what form of monitoring (view, dashboard, alerts) is expected?
What is meant by a 'team' and how are team membership and team TODO visibility determined for the team view and Team Lead role?
Which users may update TODO status: only assignees (Employee role), or also owners and Team Leads? Status values are defined only in BR-006.
What 'basic platform configuration' is within Administrator scope, and what user-management actions are included?
BR-009 (search) is marked Should while other BR items are Must; confirm whether search is required for the initial release.

What determines authorization versus permission for deleting and reassigning TODOs? BR-013 says 'where permitted' and section 7.2 says 'where authorized', and the evidence does not define who holds these rights.
How is team membership defined for Team Leads, and what does 'their team members' include?
What criteria define an Overdue TODO, and what are the permitted values and transitions for TODO status (Open, In Progress, Completed)?
What priority levels exist, and which ones count as High/Critical? The evidence refers to selecting a priority but does not list the options.
Which users can be assigned a TODO, and what is the scope of dashboard counts (own TODOs, team TODOs, or all TODOs)?
Which browsers are 'supported browsers' for the web interface requirement BR-015? No browser list or version targets are provided.
Who is permitted to approve a due date earlier than the creation date, and how is that explicit permission recorded?
What defines an 'authorized user' for assigning or modifying TODOs (roles, permissions, or ownership rules)? The evidence does not specify the authorization model.
What are the agreed NFRs that the application must meet? The supplied evidence does not include the NFR values, thresholds, or measures.
How are dashboard counts and the correctness of filtering and search results to be verified? The evidence does not define the expected counts, states, filter criteria, or search behavior.

NFR-PERF-001 refers to 'normal load' but the source does not define what constitutes normal load (for example, user count, request rate, or data volume). Should the load profile be defined so the response-time target can be tested?

NFR-PERF-002, NFR-PERF-003, and NFR-PERF-004 do not state the load condition or measurement window under which the 95% targets apply. Should these targets be assumed to apply under the same normal load as NFR-PERF-001, and over what measurement period?

NFR-PERF-005 states 'At least 500' concurrent active users without a defined time window or definition of 'active' (for example, session activity within a set period). How should concurrent active users be defined and measured for acceptance?
What maintenance windows are agreed, and how are they defined or approved? NFR-AVL-001 excludes them from the 99.5% monthly availability target without specifying them.
To whom and by what channel must planned maintenance be communicated under NFR-AVL-002?
How is 'restored' measured for NFR-AVL-003 (start and end points of the 30-minute window, and what counts as service restoration)?
What defines 'without major redesign' and what capacity target applies to 'future growth beyond initial capacity'? No quantified target is given.
What criteria determine when horizontal scalability is 'practical' for application services?
Is the 'should' obligation for auditing administrative actions mandatory or optional? What events, retention, and access requirements apply to the audit trail?
Will passwords be locally managed, or is authentication delegated to an external identity provider? This determines whether the hashing requirement applies.
Which roles exist and what TODO data does each role permit? The role-based authorization requirements reference roles that are not defined in the supplied evidence.
Is the list of common web vulnerabilities (injection, broken access control, XSS) exhaustive or illustrative? The word 'including' leaves the scope open.
What are XATA's retention policy periods and deletion rules that govern deleted TODO data? The policy is referenced but not supplied.
What step-count target defines 'minimal steps' for the core create/update/complete flow?
Which screen sizes or breakpoints define 'standard desktop and tablet screens' for the responsive UI requirement?
Which WCAG 2.1 AA success criteria are in scope, and what determines when meeting them is 'practical'?
What measurable thresholds define 'sufficient contrast' and 'readable sizing' for text?
Which components or flows are considered 'critical business logic', and what unit test coverage level is expected?
Where are correlation/request identifiers 'appropriate' in logs, and which service failures must operational alerts cover?
What backup schedule is 'agreed', who agrees it, and when is it agreed?
What constitutes a 'major failure' that triggers the restoration requirement?
How will XATA agreement to a different RPO be given, and what alternative RPO values are acceptable?
Which browsers and versions beyond Chrome and Edge are in scope, given the wording 'such as', and what defines 'current versions'?
Who approves browser-specific functionality, and what approval process applies?
Is the 'should' in the API interface requirement a mandatory obligation or a preference?
What are the XATA authorization rules and XATA data retention and deletion policies referenced, and are they supplied?
What is the testing frequency for recovery procedures ('periodically'), and who performs the testing?
What is 'XBS', and which party is responsible for documenting restoration dependencies?
The agreed NFRs referenced for production acceptance are not included in the supplied evidence. Which NFR statements, thresholds, and measurement criteria constitute the 'agreed NFRs'?

The priority table assigns Must or Should to NFR categories but gives no measurable thresholds, units, or detailed requirement statements for each category. What specific requirements sit under each category, and what do Must and Should obligations require in terms of compliance?
The acronym 'XBS' is used as the party responsible for compliance but is not defined in the supplied evidence. Which system or organization does 'XBS' refer to?
